Let me tell you about my week, because it was not a normal one. On Monday we had a system problem and the payroll almost went out late. I spent the whole morning with the finance team and we fixed it before lunch. On Tuesday I ran four interviews for one position. Four candidates in one day is too many, and by the last one I was not really listening any more. On Wednesday I did something better. I closed my laptop and I walked around the stores. I talked to eleven people. Nobody asked me about strategy. They asked me about the schedule and about the coffee machine. On Thursday I wrote the report that nobody reads. And on Friday I finally started the work I planned for Monday. That is a normal week in HR.

In every interview I ask the same simple question. Tell me about last week at work. People think it is small talk. It is not. I ask it because I want to hear three things. First, do you remember what you actually did? You would be surprised how many people cannot say it. Second, do you use the past correctly? I am not an English teacher, but when somebody says I go to a meeting yesterday, I notice it, and the story becomes harder to follow. And third, do you tell me the good part and the difficult part? Last week I finished this, and I did not finish that. That answer tells me you are honest and organised. So before your next interview, take five minutes and write your week down in English. It is the cheapest preparation there is.

Good morning, Marco. Here is my week. Last week I ran three final interviews and we closed the shortlist. We interviewed six people and we shortlisted three. I did not finish the backlog, so it moves to this week.
